subject: Proposal: economic parity + staged pilot for CloudServe replacement
messages:
From: Ben Matthews <ben@fastretail.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — pricing comparison & swap plan

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking the time on the intro call last week. As discussed, we're evaluating a potential move off CloudServe and need a clean economic comparison we can present to our CFO and procurement. Key asks: 

- Can you provide a price parity proposal that lines up with our current effective blended rate (we currently pay ~$0.0036/token average across models) but accounts for onboarding/egress/seq-length differences?
- Migration incentives we can present to execs (credits, free engineering hours, interim SLAs).
- A short phased pilot approach we can sign up to that minimizes business disruption.

Attached is our usage snapshot and the SOW template procurement prefers. Looking for a short bulleted proposal by end of week.

Thanks,
Ben

Head of Platform Engineering, FastRetail
ben@fastretail.com
+1 415-555-0189

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — pricing comparison & swap plan

Ben — appreciate the context and attached snapshot. High level proposal below (quick summary so your CFO can scan):

1) Economic parity + onboarding credits
- Effective rate: match CloudServe's blended $0.0036/token for months 1–9. For months 10–12, 6% below that blended rate (to create a retention incentive).
- Upfront migration credit: $175,000 applied to invoices over the first 12 months (to offset egress and integration cost).
- Pilot credit bucket: $25k reserved for pilot usage (first 3 months) — if pilot converts, credit rolls into month 4 invoice.

2) Pilot & rollout structure (recommended)
- Phase A (3-week tech validation): small-scale verification with your infra team — no commitment, Redwood provides 8 engineer-days for integration support (remote).
- Phase B (3-month pilot): up to 10% of current monthly token usage on matched pricing + $25k pilot credit, weekly checkpoints, and a single canary region for low-latency routing.
- Phase C (rollout): full production ramp with 30-day rollback window and automated fallback to CloudServe until we reach parity SLA metrics.

3) SLA and support
- 99.5% runtime SLA for production tier after rollout.
- Complimentary Premium Support for first 90 days (includes two assigned CS contacts and bi-weekly ops review).

4) Deliverables & timing
- We will send a redlined SOW and a migration runbook by EOD Wednesday. DocuSign link available for the pilot agreement only (no long-term commit).

If that aligns, I can loop in Legal to pre-seed the SOW and have Lauren review commercial terms you flagged. Quick question: is the CFO primarily concerned with one-time egress fees or the annual run-rate? That will help us decide whether to increase the upfront credit or deepen the per-token discount.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Looping in a couple of legal/commercial notes — drafting guidance for the SOW redline: 

- Limit migration credit usage to line items (token usage + egress) to avoid ambiguity; add example allocation table in the SOW (we'll attach a sample worksheet).
- Pilot agreement: include a 30-day termination/escape clause for both sides and specify that pilot credits are non-refundable but applied to invoices if customer converts.
- If they ask for a warranty on model parity, we should instead offer measurable acceptance criteria (latency percentiles, inference accuracy baselines for two sample prompts) and an evaluation window.

Also, Sean — suggest we offer a 2% additional discount if they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity within 60 days of pilot conversion (helps lock in Dedicated pipeline).

I'll prepare a redline SOW (FastRetail_SOW_draft.pdf) and the migration-runbook.xlsx with the allocation table — will share to the drive link Hannah referenced.

Hannah/Team — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance: 

- CFO wants to see two scenarios: (A) higher upfront credit ($250k) with a modest per-token parity for 9 months and (B) lower upfront credit ($100k) but a 9–12 month deeper per-token discount (10% below blended). Can you sketch that as an either/or on the SOW?
- Procurement asked that any pilot agreement include explicit data handling commitments and a short audit window for logs retention (we'll provide SOC 2 scope questions).
- Fast question: can Redwood guarantee no surprise egress charges for the pilot period if we keep ingress/egress under 5TB?

We can run the pilot starting Nov 16 if you can get the engineer availability confirmed.

Best,
Ben

Ben — great, thank you. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Alternate scenarios: we'll table A and B in the SOW cover sheet so you can present both to CFO. Scenario A: $250k migration credit, parity for months 1–9, month 10–12 at 3% below blended. Scenario B: $100k migration credit, months 1–12 at 10% below blended. Both include the $25k pilot credit.

2) Egress guarantees: we will cap pilot egress charges at $0 for the first 5TB as long as usage stays within the pilot bucket and we have pre-notified routes for bulk exports. We'll call this an "egress allowance" in the pilot agreement; any overage will be billed at published rates after written notice.

3) Security & logs: we will provide a SOC 2 evidence bundle and a 14-day audit logs snapshot for the pilot period (they can request extended retention as an add-on).

4) Timing & resource confirmation: engineering can support kickoff Nov 16 — I'll send the pilot DocuSign (pilot-only) and the redline SOW to your procurement contact by EOD tomorrow.
